messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE: High OOM/error spike on runtime-prod-gpu (cluster: rtp-gpu-02). Incident ID INC-2026-1537. Symptoms: increased 500s, worker restarts, degraded latency. Paging oncall @alice (first responder). Please ack and triage.
alice (oncall): acked. I'm looking. Any immediate customer-impact notes?
emily (support): We have 3 customers reporting elevated error rates on embeddings endpoints. CS ticket numbers: #4501, #4502. Noting increased latency spikes at 12:23 UTC.
ben (sre): seeing repeated oom logs on machine rtp-gpu-02-[07,08]. Kernel: out-of-memory: kill process 21345 (runtime) Killed
carmen (runtime): joining. Hypothesis: KV cache growth combined with large batch sizes causing fragmentation. Will pull GPU mem stats.
alice (oncall): can we drop batch size for that pool asap? devon can we scale to spare capacity (rtp-gpu-03) while we debug?
devon (mlops): triggering scale-up and moving some routes off pool via routing policy. `routed_off = /models/*/embeddings` for canary. ETA ~3m.
ben (sre): past 30m GPU mem summary (from node exporter):
```
node rtp-gpu-02-07: GPU0 total 48GB used 46.8GB alloc 45.9GB free 1.2GB
node rtp-gpu-02-08: GPU0 total 48GB used 47.2GB alloc 46.6GB free 0.8GB
cache kv_entries: 1.2M -> growth observed after 12:15 UTC
OOM events: 12:21:34, 12:24:02, 12:26:19
```
carmen (runtime): logs also show KV cache miss storms causing rehydration leading to big prefixes in KV cache. We might be keeping stale entries per session. Patch idea: aggressive TTL + trim on large sessions.
alice (oncall): mitigation checklist: 1) scale up/spill routes (devon) 2) reduce per-request batch_size to 1 on affected route (alice) 3) evict KV cache candidates older than 10m (carmen) 4) collect timeline and logs (ben)
ben (sre): applying filters to get timeline. Sharing aggregated log chunk (snip):
```
12:20:58 WARN runtime: kvcache miss session=abcd user=svc-22
12:21:00 INFO runtime: start batch size=16 model=redwood-open-1
12:21:34 ERROR runtime: OOM alloc_bytes=123456789
12:22:10 INFO runtime: worker restart id=rtw-934
```
emily (support): customers seeing 5xx ratio go from 0.2% -> 8% during window. Notable spike between 12:20-12:28 UTC.
carmen (runtime): quick mitigation deployed: set `KV_CACHE_TRIM_THRESHOLD=0.6` and `KV_ENTRY_TTL_SECONDS=600` for rtp-gpu-02 pool. Also lowering `DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE=1` for embeddings route via in-flight feature flag.
alice (oncall): applied `DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE=1` on route. Monitoring.
devon (mlops): traffic shifted to rtp-gpu-03 and dedicated warm standby. No failures on new nodes so far. Routing change id: route-shift-1856.
ben (sre): post-mitigation GPU memory (12:35 UTC):
```
rtp-gpu-02-07 used 42.1GB free 5.9GB
rtp-gpu-02-08 used 43.0GB free 5.0GB
kv_entries: stabilized at 320k
```
frank (pm): any estimate for customer impact window so we can update status page?
emily (support): primary impact window ~12:20-12:33 UTC. We'll publish an update: "intermittent 500s during 12:20-12:33 UTC, mitigated by routing and config changes."
alice (oncall): next steps for RCA in-thread: 1) collect full node allocator traces (carmen/ben) 2) dump KV cache histogram + top heavy keys (carmen) 3) rerun reproducer with long-tail sessions and batch 16 locally (devon)
carmen (runtime): starting profiler and collecting allocator traces now. Also saving `nvprof` style traces from the hot worker.
ben (sre): I'm uploading syslogs + `dmesg` and `runtime` stderr to the incident storage: gs://redwood-incidents/INC-2026-1537/logs.tar.gz
alice (oncall): documenting timeline in incident doc. Adding hypothesis tags: [kv-cache-growth], [batching], [fragmentation].
frank (pm): flagging this for postmortem; include customer-facing timeline and mitigation steps. Priority P2.
devon (mlops): repro attempt with synthetic load: simulating 200 concurrent sessions with occasional long-prefixs. Reproducer run shows memory growth after ~220s when default batch 16 + KV rehydration enabled.
carmen (runtime): hypothesis update: not a single giant leak; looks like fragmentation + delayed freeing of reserved KV buffers + large batches triggering allocations beyond immediate reclaim. Two levers helped: smaller batches (reduces peak alloc) and trimming stale KV entries (reduces live set).
ben (sre): will correlate allocator free latency with restart timestamps. If fragmentation high, next steps: 1) change allocation strategy, 2) introduce periodic compaction, 3) avoid large contiguous allocations.
alice (oncall): handing off to ben/carmen for deep RCA. I'm offcall in 45m; if anything spikes, page SRE team. ben/carmen pls own follow-ups. I'll file the initial postmortem draft.
incident-bot: NOTE: oncall handoff scheduled at 13:00 UTC to ben (sre). Reminder: update incident status when resolved.
carmen (runtime): acknowledged. We'll push an experimental compaction job to canary pool tomorrow and test increased KV eviction heuristics.
ben (sre): attaching short log excerpt for the timeline to the incident doc. Also adding a hashmap of top 20 KV keys by size.
emily (support): posting status page update now. Will link to postmortem when available.
frank (pm): thanks all — appreciate the quick mitigation. We'll want a runbook update for 'kv cache growth + high batch size' scenarios.
alice (oncall): closing immediate page. handoff complete. follow-ups in INC-2026-1537-rca doc. :white_check_mark:
file_description: In-incident coordination and RCA thread: runtime OOM/fragmentation affecting KV cache and batching, includes mitigation steps, logs, and handoff
